title: Regularity of a ring map is local on the target
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to\Lambda$ be a ring map of commutative rings with $\Lambda$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ with $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ write $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, $r/s\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(s)$, for the induced map of localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The following are equivalent: (1) $\varphi$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]; (2) $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$, $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$; (3) $\varphi_{\mathfrak m'}:R_{\mathfrak m}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak m'}$ is regular for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'\subset\Lambda$, $\mathfrak m=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m')$ (a prime ideal of $R$).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C0 (lemma-regular-local, line 10390); its proof cites Algebra Definition 00OD (regular ring: all local rings regular) and Algebra Lemma 00HT (lemma-flat-localization)

proof.text: For a prime q of S, the composite R -> S -> S_q is regular by regular composition and regularity of localization maps. Its fibres are Noetherian because S_q is Noetherian. Give S_q its R_p-algebra structure through the canonical local ring map, where p = q.comap f. The scalar-tower identity is Localization.localRingHom_to_map. Regularity through source localization now proves R_p -> S_q regular.

Suppose all the maps R_r -> S_m for maximal m are regular. They are flat. Flatness of R_r over R and transitivity make S_m flat over R. Module.flat_of_isLocalized_maximal applied to the S-module S then proves S flat over R. This is the maximal-target version of the flat local criterion and works with independent universes for R and S.

For each maximal m, the composite R -> R_r -> S_m is regular by regularity of localization maps and regular composition; its fibres are Noetherian by the Noetherian-target fibre theorem. Thus for each fixed source prime p, the fibre of R -> S_m is geometrically regular for every maximal m. Apply the fixed-fibre descent theorem to conclude that the fibre of R -> S at p is geometrically regular. Together with the flatness already proved, this gives regularity of f.

Every maximal ideal is prime, so the prime-local hypothesis specializes to the maximal-local hypothesis. Use the forward implication and the maximal-local converse just established to assemble both equivalences.

proof_origin.note: Lean reduction of Stacks 07C0: use existing regular-composition and regular-through-localization statements for localization, prove maximal flat descent directly, and split only the fixed-fibre geometric descent argument.
